title: Ardengard version 1: product requirements
problem: Grok Bot, Muse, dots and Cue sell a team of AI coworkers with their own computers, but they are closed, run on the vendor's cloud and hold your data.
The open-source alternatives (OpenMausBot, OpenClaw, Hermes) are young, rebuild their own chat apps, and shipped serious security holes in 2026.
Builders in your community want a team of agents they can run themselves, understand, and trust, without writing a chat app.

users.need: Build it in public, run it for demos and content, show what works and what does not, with real numbers.
Install one package on their own server, get a safe working bot team in an hour, and extend it with their own skills.

goals: One install brings up a Buzz workspace with at least one Claude Code bot that answers in channels and threads.
Bots learn through skill files and remember through plain-file memory they can show and forget.
Every risky action waits for approval; safe defaults ship on; nothing listens on the public internet.
Every job records its real value: time you estimated against time you spent reviewing and fixing.
A newcomer goes from a fresh server to a first finished job in under one hour by following the docs.
non_goals: Our own chat app or phone app (Buzz and Telegram cover version 1).
Bot email addresses, phone numbers, wallets or payments.
Teaching by demonstration, a knowledge graph, agent-to-agent (A2A) links, multi-tenant hosting.

architecture.summary: We do not build a chat app or an agent loop. Buzz provides the workspace; Buzz's own connector runs Claude Code as a Buzz member; our code is the layer that makes bots safe, useful and measurable.

parts.role: Workspace: channels, threads, DMs, search, signed audit log.
parts.source: Official image ghcr.io/block/buzz pinned by release and digest, with Postgres, Redis and MinIO

parts.role: Connects a bot to Buzz: listens for mentions, prompts the agent, posts replies. Defaults to answering only its owner.
Runs Claude Code as an ACP agent that buzz-acp can drive.
One folder per bot in git: instructions, skills, tools, model, permissions.
Permission broker for every tool call: allow lists, never-delegate list, untrusted-content quarantine, one-writer rule, caps, kill switch.
parts.source: Ours, using Claude Code hooks and permission callbacks

parts.role: MCP server over markdown fact files and SQLite full-text search: add, update, delete or skip; scopes; unverified flag; nightly tidy.
A sandboxed Linux desktop with a browser, driven through Cua, for website work.
Telegram bot that answers only you: short notices and approve or deny buttons; no sensitive content.
Per-job estimate, review time, rework, cost and OpenTelemetry traces.
parts.source: Ours plus a self-hosted trace viewer

parts.role: One Docker Compose stack with Tailscale, backups and update with rollback.

requirements.text: docker compose up on Ubuntu 24.04 starts Buzz, one bot and all its services; the server refuses to start on a public address.
A bot appears in Buzz as a member with its own key, answers @mentions in channels, threads and DMs, and answers only its owner by default.
Each bot is defined by a folder in git; a change runs the bot's tests before it goes live; one command rolls back.
Bots load skill files in the Agent Skills format; a bot may propose a skill edit, which needs your approval and must pass the skill's tests.
Bots read and write memory only through the memory server; every fact has source, date, scope and expiry; you can list, edit and forget facts.
Each turn gets the core profile, the task, retrieved facts and only the tools the job needs; long sessions end with a handoff note and restart fresh.
New bots start read-only with Ask on every action; irreversible actions always wait for you; a bot that read untrusted content cannot send or change settings in that turn.
Secrets are used through a broker and never enter a model's context, a transcript or a log.
For any task exactly one bot writes; others may only advise.
A Telegram bot that answers only your user ID sends notices and approve or deny buttons and never includes client names, money, health or credentials.
A bot can use a sandboxed desktop with a browser for website work; you can watch it and take over.
A job keeps a progress file, survives a restart and resumes; a job with no progress for 20 minutes is reported.
Nothing a bot makes is sent to another person until a reviewer step marks it complete.
Every job records a trace with steps, time, tokens and cost, viewable in a self-hosted viewer.
Every job records your estimate before and your review and fix time after; the scorecard shows wins and losses.
A Pause all control stops every bot and revokes sessions; daily caps on usage and messages per bot.
Nightly encrypted backups to storage you own; one command restores, exports everything, or deletes a scope.
Apache 2.0 license, SECURITY.md, signed releases with a changelog, docs that take a newcomer to a first job in under an hour.

nonfunctional: Runs on a 4 vCPU, 16 GB server with one shared bot desktop; the minimum is measured in phase 0.
Reachable only over Tailscale; no public ports.
Every dependency, image, MCP server and skill pinned by version and digest.
Files 0600 and folders 0700; the build fails on readable secrets.
/sec-ship on every PR; /redteam against a local instance before each release.
metrics: Install to first finished job: under 60 minutes for a newcomer following the docs.
Benchmark jobs used without rework: at least 3 of 5 by release 1.
Actions that ran without required approval: zero, tested every release.
Your review and fix time below your own estimate on at least half of benchmark runs.

risks.risk: Buzz is a developer preview; approval gates and phone apps are unfinished.
risks.plan: Phase 0 spike; pin a release; fallback interface from the mockup if Buzz fails the check.

risks.risk: How buzz-acp handles Claude Code permission requests is unknown.
risks.plan: Phase 0 spike decides whether approvals flow through Buzz, Telegram or both.

risks.risk: Bots share your Claude plan limits.
risks.plan: Daily caps per bot; a separate account or API key decided in phase 0.

risks.risk: Community members run it carelessly and expose it.
risks.plan: Refuse public addresses, safe defaults, plain-language security docs.

risks.risk: It feels useful but is not.
risks.plan: Value log and benchmark from the first job; publish losses too.

open_questions: Separate Claude account or API key for bots, or your subscription with caps?
Accept outside pull requests from day one, or publish as a reference build first?
Workflow engine (Temporal, Hatchet) or a SQLite job table for version 1?
